chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a believer who killed a Nāṣibī man, known for enmity, on account of his religion, out of anger for Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: is he to be killed in retaliation for him? He said: "As for these people, they would kill him for him; but if it were referred to a just Imam, he would not kill him in retaliation for him." I said: Then is his blood to be disregarded? He said: "No. But if he has heirs, it is upon the Imam to give them the blood-money from the Bayt al-Māl, because his killer only killed him out of anger for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and for the Imam, and for the religion of the Muslims."

key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَادِلٍ: a just Imam; the legitimate authority who judges correctly
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money; financial compensation due in a homicide case
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury from which compensation is paid
key_terms.غَضَبًا لِلَّهِ: out of anger for Allah; indicating the motive attributed in the case
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer; the Muslim perpetrator in the legal case
key_terms.نَاصِبًا: a Nāṣibī; one known for enmity toward Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and the religion
key_terms.وَرَثَةٌ: heirs; those entitled to receive the blood-money

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a believer kills a Nāṣibī known for enmity to the religion according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling concerning a believer who kills a Nāṣibī known for his enmity toward the religion. Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام states that a just Imam would not impose retaliation upon the killer, yet the victim’s blood is not nullified, and any due blood-money for heirs is to be paid from the Bayt al-Māl.
